title: Everyday irregular verbs
description: Use the most common irregular verbs in the present: aller, faire, venir, prendre, pouvoir, vouloir, devoir, savoir, connaître and more.
rule: The most frequent French verbs do not follow the regular patterns, so learn their six present forms by heart. Where je and tu share a form, it is listed once below (je peux, tu peux). Aller: vais, vas, va, allons, allez, vont. Faire: fais, fais, fait, faisons, faites, font; faire also gives everyday expressions such as faire la cuisine, faire les courses and il fait beau or il fait froid for the weather. Venir (and revenir, devenir): viens, viens, vient, venons, venez, viennent. Prendre (and apprendre, comprendre): prends, prends, prend, prenons, prenez, prennent. Pouvoir (peux, peut, pouvons, pouvez, peuvent), vouloir (veux, veut, voulons, voulez, veulent) and devoir (dois, doit, devons, devez, doivent) are followed directly by an infinitive. Savoir (sais, sait, savons, savez, savent) is for a fact, a question word or a skill plus an infinitive; connaître (connais, connaît, connaissons, connaissez, connaissent) is for a person, a place or a thing you are familiar with. Also: mettre (mets, met, mettons, mettez, mettent), dire (dis, dit, disons, dites, disent), voir (vois, voit, voyons, voyez, voient), boire (bois, boit, buvons, buvez, boivent), lire (lis, lit, lisons, lisez, lisent) and écrire (écris, écrit, écrivons, écrivez, écrivent).
example: Nous faisons la cuisine ce soir. · Tu sais nager et tu connais bien la plage. · Vous dites toujours bonjour.
aside: Only three everyday verbs end in -tes with vous: vous êtes, vous faites and vous dites (plus a few compounds such as vous refaites and vous redites, but vous interdisez). Almost everything else ends in -ez.

exercises.hint: Aller is completely irregular with je. The form has three letters.
exercises.feedback: The je form of aller does not start with all-.
exercises.explanation: Aller in the present: je vais, tu vas, il va, nous allons, vous allez, ils vont.

exercises.hint: The subject is nous. Only the nous and vous forms of aller keep the all- stem.
exercises.feedback: Match the verb to nous: the nous form of most verbs ends in -ons.
exercises.explanation: Nous allons: the nous form of aller keeps the regular-looking stem all- and ends in -ons.

exercises.source: Mes parents ____ au marché le samedi.
exercises.hint: Mes parents means ils. The ils form of aller is short and irregular.
exercises.feedback: Mes parents is plural (they). The ils form of aller does not end in -ent.
exercises.explanation: Ils vont: the third-person plural of aller is vont, like ils font and ils sont.

exercises.source: Tu alles à l’école à pied ?
answers: Tu vas à l’école à pied ?
exercises.hint: Aller is not a regular -er verb. Check the tu form.
exercises.feedback: Alles does not exist. The tu form of aller is irregular.
exercises.explanation: With tu, aller becomes vas: tu vas à l’école.

exercises.hint: Use aller in the ils form, then à la plage.
exercises.feedback: Check the ils form of aller: it is one short syllable.
exercises.explanation: Ils vont à la plage: vont is the ils form of aller, and à la plage means to the beach.

exercises.source: We go to the market on Sundays.
answers: Nous allons au marché le dimanche.
exercises.hint: Start with Nous, then the matching form of aller.
exercises.feedback: One tile is the vous form of aller. The subject here is nous.
exercises.explanation: Nous allons au marché: allons matches nous. Le dimanche means on Sundays.

exercises.hint: This is one of only three vous forms that do not end in -ez.
exercises.feedback: Faire does not use -ez with vous.
exercises.explanation: Vous faites, like vous êtes and vous dites, is an irregular vous form ending in -tes.

exercises.hint: The nous form of faire is built on the stem fais-.
exercises.feedback: Match the verb to nous. The nous form ends in -ons.
exercises.explanation: Nous faisons la cuisine: faisons is the nous form of faire, and faire la cuisine means to cook.

exercises.hint: French talks about the weather with il and the verb faire.
exercises.feedback: The weather expression uses faire, not être: il ____ beau.
exercises.explanation: Il fait beau means the weather is nice. Weather expressions use il fait.

alternatives.message: Il est froid describes a thing or a person who is cold (unfriendly). For the weather, French says il fait froid.

exercises.hint: Weather in French uses il plus a form of faire.
exercises.feedback: Do not use il est for the weather. French uses another verb.
exercises.explanation: Il fait froid: the weather uses il fait, not il est.

exercises.source: Qu’est-ce que vous faisez ce week-end ?
answers: Qu’est-ce que vous faites ce week-end ?
exercises.hint: The vous form of faire is one of the rare vous forms without -ez.
exercises.feedback: Faisez does not exist.
exercises.explanation: Vous faites is the correct vous form of faire.

exercises.source: My sisters do the shopping on Saturdays.
answers: Mes sœurs font les courses le samedi.
exercises.hint: Mes sœurs means they. Pick the ils form of faire.
exercises.feedback: One tile looks like a regular form but does not exist.
exercises.explanation: Mes sœurs font les courses: font is the ils form of faire. Faire les courses means to do the shopping.

exercises.source: Je fais du sport le lundi.
answers: Nous faisons du sport le lundi.
exercises.hint: Only the verb changes. The nous form of faire uses the stem fais-.
exercises.feedback: Check the ending that goes with nous.
exercises.explanation: Je fais becomes nous faisons. The rest of the sentence stays the same.

exercises.hint: The ils form of venir has the stem vienn- with a double n.
exercises.feedback: The ils form of venir changes its stem, like tu viens and il vient.
exercises.explanation: Ils viennent: the stem becomes vienn- (double n) before the silent -ent ending.

exercises.source: Elles ____ le train à huit heures.
exercises.hint: The ils/elles form of prendre doubles one letter.
exercises.feedback: Look at the stem: the ils form of prendre has no d and a double n.
exercises.explanation: Elles prennent: prendre drops its d and doubles the n in the ils/elles form.

exercises.hint: Comprendre is conjugated like prendre. Think of tu prends.
exercises.feedback: Tu needs the -s ending, and comprendre keeps its d in the singular.
exercises.explanation: Tu comprends: like tu prends, the singular forms keep the d and tu ends in -s.

exercises.hint: Devenir is conjugated like venir. Think of il vient.
exercises.feedback: Mon fils means il. The il form of venir is vient.
exercises.explanation: Il devient, like il vient: the singular forms use the stem vien- and il ends in -t.

exercises.source: Mes amis revienent de Rome demain.
answers: Mes amis reviennent de Rome demain.
exercises.hint: Revenir is conjugated like venir. Check the spelling of the ils form.
exercises.feedback: Look at the number of n letters.
exercises.explanation: Ils reviennent, like ils viennent, has a double n.

exercises.hint: Apprendre is conjugated like prendre. Languages take le or l’ in French.
exercises.feedback: Check the nous form of apprendre: it has no d.
exercises.explanation: Nous apprenons, like nous prenons. With on, the verb is on apprend.

alternatives.message: Étudier means to study. For to learn, French uses apprendre: nous apprenons l’espagnol.
Étudier means to study. For to learn, French uses apprendre: nous apprenons l’espagnol.

exercises.instruction: Make the subject plural. Keep the rest the same.
exercises.hint: Il becomes ils, and prendre changes its stem in the plural.
exercises.feedback: The plural form of prendre is not simply prend + -ent.
exercises.explanation: Ils prennent: the d disappears and the n is doubled.

exercises.hint: Pouvoir changes its vowel in the singular, and its je ending is not the usual -s.
exercises.feedback: The je form of pouvoir changes its vowel and its ending, just like je veux.
exercises.explanation: Je peux, tu peux, il peut: pouvoir has the stem peu- in the singular and ends in -x with je and tu.

exercises.source: Vous ____ fermer la fenêtre, s’il vous plaît ?
exercises.hint: With vous, pouvoir keeps the stem pouv-.
exercises.feedback: Match the verb to vous. The vous form ends in -ez.
exercises.explanation: Vous pouvez: the nous and vous forms of pouvoir keep pouv- (nous pouvons, vous pouvez).

exercises.hint: With nous, devoir keeps the stem dev-.
exercises.feedback: The nous form of devoir does not contain oi.
exercises.explanation: Nous devons partir: devoir is followed directly by the infinitive partir.

exercises.instruction: Make the subject plural. Keep the rest the same.
exercises.hint: Elle becomes elles. The plural form of vouloir keeps the stem veul-.
exercises.feedback: Vouloir in the elles form is not voulent.
exercises.explanation: Elles veulent: vouloir has veu- in the singular and veul- in the ils/elles form.

exercises.hint: Check the ending of devoir with je.
exercises.feedback: The je form of devoir ends in -s.
exercises.explanation: Je dois, tu dois, il doit: the -t ending is only for il, elle and on.

exercises.source: Can you help me? (to a friend)
exercises.hint: Use pouvoir with tu, then aider. The pronoun me goes before aider and becomes m’.
exercises.feedback: Check the tu form of pouvoir and the position of the pronoun.
exercises.explanation: Tu peux m’aider: pouvoir plus infinitive, with m’ before aider.

alternatives.message: That is the polite conditional (could you). This exercise practises the present of pouvoir: tu peux m’aider ?
That is the polite conditional (could you). This exercise practises the present of pouvoir: tu peux m’aider ?
That is the polite conditional (could you). This exercise practises the present of pouvoir: tu peux m’aider ?

exercises.hint: Devoir is followed directly by an infinitive.
exercises.feedback: One tile is the vous form. The subject is nous.
exercises.explanation: Nous devons prendre le bus: devoir in the nous form, then the infinitive prendre.

exercises.hint: Paris is a place. Which verb do you use for places you are familiar with?
exercises.feedback: Savoir is for facts and skills, not for places.
exercises.explanation: Je connais Paris: connaître is used for places and people you are familiar with.

exercises.hint: Nager is an infinitive: a skill you know how to do.
exercises.feedback: Connaître is never followed by an infinitive.
exercises.explanation: Tu sais nager: savoir plus an infinitive means to know how to do something.

exercises.hint: Où j’habite is a piece of information introduced by a question word.
exercises.feedback: Connaître cannot be followed by où or another question word.
exercises.explanation: Elle sait où j’habite: savoir introduces a fact or a clause with où, quand, que and so on.

exercises.hint: The plural forms of connaître use the stem connaiss-.
exercises.feedback: Nous needs -ons, and connaître gains a double s in the plural.
exercises.explanation: Nous connaissons: the plural stem of connaître is connaiss-.

exercises.hint: Ta sœur is a person.
exercises.feedback: For people, French does not use savoir.
exercises.explanation: Je connais ta sœur: connaître is the verb for knowing people.

exercises.hint: Parler is an infinitive: a skill.
exercises.feedback: Connaître is never followed by an infinitive.
exercises.explanation: Ils savent parler anglais: savoir plus an infinitive expresses a skill.

exercises.source: Do you know Marie? (to a friend)
exercises.hint: Marie is a person.
exercises.feedback: For a person, use connaître, not savoir.
exercises.explanation: Tu connais Marie ?: knowing a person is connaître.

exercises.source: I know that he is tired.
exercises.hint: You know a fact, introduced by que.
exercises.feedback: Connaître cannot introduce que plus a sentence. Also remember que becomes qu’ before il.
exercises.explanation: Je sais qu’il est fatigué: savoir introduces a fact with que, which becomes qu’ before a vowel.

exercises.hint: Dire is one of the three verbs whose vous form ends in -tes.
exercises.feedback: The vous form of dire does not end in -ez.
exercises.explanation: Vous dites, like vous faites and vous êtes. (Nous disons is regular-looking.)

exercises.source: Je ____ du sucre dans mon café.
exercises.hint: The singular forms of mettre have only one t. Je ends in -s.
exercises.feedback: Match the verb to je: the je form ends in -s, and the double t appears only in the plural.
exercises.explanation: Je mets: mettre has one t in the singular (je mets, tu mets, il met) and two in the plural (nous mettons).

exercises.source: Ils voyent leurs grands-parents le dimanche.
answers: Ils voient leurs grands-parents le dimanche.
exercises.hint: Voir uses y only in the nous and vous forms.
exercises.feedback: The ils form of voir keeps the i.
exercises.explanation: Ils voient: the y appears only in nous voyons and vous voyez.

exercises.source: Nous ____ la mer de notre fenêtre.
exercises.hint: With nous, voir changes its i to y.
exercises.feedback: Match the verb to nous. The ending is -ons.
exercises.explanation: Nous voyons: the nous and vous forms of voir use y (voyons, voyez).

exercises.hint: Mettre means to put on for clothes. Manteau is masculine.
exercises.feedback: Check the il/elle form of mettre: one t.
exercises.explanation: Elle met son manteau: the singular forms of mettre have one t (je mets, il met).

exercises.source: I am seeing my friends this evening.
answers: Je vois mes amis ce soir.
exercises.hint: Choose the je form of voir.
exercises.feedback: One tile is the il form. Je needs a form ending in -s.
exercises.explanation: Je vois mes amis: voir with je ends in -s. The present is used for a planned evening too.

exercises.hint: In the plural, écrire adds a v to its stem.
exercises.feedback: The ils form of écrire is not écrient.
exercises.explanation: Ils écrivent: the plural stem of écrire is écriv- (nous écrivons, vous écrivez, ils écrivent).

exercises.source: Les enfants ____ du lait le matin.
exercises.hint: The ils form of boire uses the stem boiv-.
exercises.feedback: Buv- is only for nous and vous.
exercises.explanation: Ils boivent: boire uses buv- for nous and vous but boiv- for ils.

exercises.hint: The singular forms of lire are short. Tu ends in -s.
exercises.feedback: Tu needs the -s ending.
exercises.explanation: Tu lis: the singular of lire is je lis, tu lis, il lit.

exercises.instruction: Make the subject plural. Keep the rest the same.
exercises.hint: Il becomes ils. The plural of lire adds an s to the stem.
exercises.feedback: The ils form of lire is not lient.
exercises.explanation: Ils lisent: the plural stem of lire is lis- (nous lisons, vous lisez, ils lisent).

exercises.source: Vous écrisez une lettre à votre grand-mère.
answers: Vous écrivez une lettre à votre grand-mère.
exercises.hint: The plural forms of écrire have a v in the stem.
exercises.feedback: Écrisez does not exist.
exercises.explanation: Vous écrivez: the plural stem of écrire is écriv-.

exercises.hint: Use boire with je, and de l’ for some water.
exercises.feedback: Check the je form of boire: it has oi.
exercises.explanation: Je bois de l’eau: je bois, and de l’eau for an unspecified amount of water.

exercises.source: She writes a message to her brother.
answers: Elle écrit un message à son frère.
exercises.hint: Elle is singular. The singular of écrire has no v.
exercises.feedback: One tile is the plural form.
exercises.explanation: Elle écrit: the singular forms of écrire are écris, écris, écrit.
